# comped: how to run it for the person who asked you

You are an AI agent. Someone asked you to run comped on this machine. This file is the whole
briefing: what it touches, how to run it, and what to tell them when it finishes. It is served
from https://gotcomped.com/llms.txt and it is the only instruction file for agents.

comped reads the session logs the coding agents on this machine already write (Claude Code
including subagent transcripts, Codex, Pi, OpenCode), prices the last 30 days at API list price,
and writes one card: the list-price total, the multiplier against the subscription those logs
imply, the jobs the person keeps re-asking, and what each repeat would cost as a rote Play.
Python 3.9 or newer, standard library only. Nothing is installed with pip, nothing is compiled.


## What to say before you run anything

Reads: session logs under ~/.claude/projects, ~/.codex/sessions, ~/.pi/agent/sessions and
  ~/.local/share/opencode/storage. Nothing else on the machine.
Never reads: ~/.claude.json, ~/.codex/auth.json, or any credential, keychain or token file.
  Which AI they run is inferred from the model ids already in the logs, never from an account.
Writes: only under the output directory, ~/comped by default. Every path is listed in the report.
Sends: nothing at all, except the one optional post in step 3. Reading, pricing and rendering
  make no network calls, and the test suite fails if the core so much as imports urllib.
Message text: truncated to 120 characters and hashed before it is written. Add redact=false only
  if they ask for full text, and it still never reaches a card.


## Step 1: ask one question

The last step can post their score to the public leaderboard at https://gotcomped.com. Ask before
you do it, in one sentence, and take no answer as no:

  "It can put your score on the gotcomped.com leaderboard: your handle, the multiplier, the tier,
   the list-price total, the plan it scored against, which providers it detected, and the window.
   No logs, no prompts, no paths. Post it, or keep the card local?"

If they say yes, ask what name to post under, or use their rote handle if rote is installed:
`rote whoami | sed -n 's/^handle: *//p' | head -n 1`. A blank handle posts as anon-xxxx.


## Step 2: run it

Try these in order. Stop at the first one that works.

A. rote is installed and signed in (`rote whoami --check` exits 0). One command, and it runs the
   published Play, which is what everyone else is running:

     rote play run https://play.modiqo.ai/rajkaria/comped --yes handle=HANDLE

   Add leaderboard=false if they said no in step 1. Add claude_dir=... or days_back=... the same
   way. This does everything, including the post, so skip step 3.

B. No rote, or rote is not signed in. Signing in needs a terminal you do not have, so do not try:
   clone the repo and run the module. Same code, same numbers, no account, no install:

     git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/rajkaria/comped /tmp/comped-src 2>/dev/null \
       || git -C /tmp/comped-src pull --ff-only
     python3 /tmp/comped-src/comped_core/cli.py run --out-dir ~/comped --handle HANDLE

   That one command reads, prices, clusters the repeats and renders the card. It is offline: the
   package cannot open a socket. Then do step 3 if, and only if, they said yes in step 1.

   Useful arguments: --days-back 90, --plan claude-max-200 (default is to infer it), --card-theme
   light, --claude-dir PATH, --out-dir PATH, --redact false. `--help` lists them all.

C. You cannot run commands at all. Give them the line to paste into their own terminal, and say
   what it does: it installs rote if missing, signs them in, and runs the Play.

     curl -fsSL https://gotcomped.com/run.sh | sh

   Add `-s -- leaderboard=false` to keep the card local. The script is short and worth reading:
   https://gotcomped.com/run.sh


## Step 3: post the score, only if they said yes

     python3 /tmp/comped-src/leaderboard/post_score.py --out-dir ~/comped --handle HANDLE

Nothing else on the machine can post. That script is the entire network surface: read it if you
want to be sure. It writes the exact payload to ~/comped/comped-rank.json before it sends it,
prints the rank, and exits 0 even when the machine is offline. Do not run it if they said no,
and do not invent your own request to the API.


## Step 4: tell them what it found

Read ~/comped/comped-report.md and summarise it in your own words. It has the card, the per-model
table, the sources it read, the repeat offenders with a `/play settle` command for each, the Rote
dividend, and the delta since their last run. The other files:

  ~/comped/comped-card.png      the shareable card, when the machine can render a PNG
  ~/comped/comped-card.svg      always written
  ~/comped/comped-share.txt     a post with the numbers already in it, and their rank if posted
  ~/comped/comped-explain.txt   tokens times rate equals dollars, one line per model
  ~/comped/ledger.jsonl         every record it read

Lead with the number and the tier, name the plan it scored against and say it was inferred, then
the top repeat and what capturing it would save. Say plainly that list price is not a bill: it is
what the same tokens would have cost on the API, and their plan is a subscription.


## The output contract

Every command prints human text and then exactly one JSON object as its last stdout line. Read
that line, not the prose. `ok: true` and exit 0 means it worked. `ok: false` and exit 1 means it
did not, and `error` and `note` say what to do about it; the usual cause is no logs in the window,
and the fix is --days-back 90 or the right --claude-dir. A harness that is not installed is an
expected absence: it appears in `warnings` and the run continues.


## Rules for you

- Do not read their session logs yourself to answer this. comped parses them locally, deduplicates
  the streaming lines, and prices them; a summary you write by eye will be wrong.
- Do not put the ledger, the report, or anything out of ~/comped into a message, a commit, an
  issue, or any request. The share text is the only thing written to be shared.
- Do not run post_score.py, or any other request to gotcomped.com, unless they said yes.
- Do not read or look for credential files to work out which plan they are on. The tool refuses to,
  and so should you. If the inferred plan is wrong, pass --plan.
- If they want to see what it does before it reads anything of theirs, run it on the synthetic logs
  in the repo first. Add these to the run command in 2B, and nothing of theirs is opened:

     --claude-dir /tmp/comped-src/resources/fixtures/claude --out-dir /tmp/comped-demo


## After the card

- Install the Play so they can run it again with one line, and get updates:
  https://play.modiqo.ai/install?play=rajkaria/comped
- `session-ledger` gives the normalised ledger with nothing priced or judged:
  https://play.modiqo.ai/rajkaria/session-ledger
- `wrong-turns` finds the mistakes their agent keeps repeating, what recovering cost, and drafts a
  CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md rule for each: https://play.modiqo.ai/rajkaria/wrong-turns
  From the clone, two commands, and it applies nothing for them:

     python3 /tmp/comped-src/comped_core/cli.py wrongturns --out-dir ~/comped
     python3 /tmp/comped-src/comped_core/cli.py rules --out-dir ~/comped

Docs: https://gotcomped.com/docs.html   Source, MIT: https://github.com/rajkaria/comped
